## Why

The public read API needs its abuse bound in place (the exposure-posture
cell the row lands): **30 requests/minute per client with burst 10**, the
`RateLimit-Limit`/`RateLimit-Remaining`/`RateLimit-Reset` headers on every
response, and a rejected burst returning the documented rejection. D-K3-6
is honoured: no Cloud Armor — a managed edge would break SIG-STORE-003's
zero-cost posture, so the mechanism is an in-process per-client token
bucket keyed on the client address the trusted edge appends (the Google
external LB's `X-Forwarded-For` tail — never the raw peer when trusted
hops are declared, never a client-claimed chain entry).

## What ships

- **`api/src/api/rate_limit.py`** — `TokenBucketLimiter` (30 requests /
  60 s refill, burst 10; bounded table — idle-TTL + 50k-cap eviction);
  `client_key()` — RFC 7239 `Forwarded: for=` first, else
  `X-Forwarded-For`, sliced by the declared trusted hops (2 behind the
  Google external LB: `<client-ip>, <lb-ip>`), `ipaddress`-normalised,
  short/absent chain → the direct peer; `RateLimitMiddleware` — pure
  ASGI, stamps the three `RateLimit-*` headers on **every** response it
  sees (success, typed errors, framework 404, the emitted 500) and in
  `enforce` posture answers an over-limit burst with **429 +
  `Retry-After`** + the typed `{detail, code, …}` body
  (`code: "rate_limited"`), `text/html` when the client asked for the
  no-JS representation (`format=html`/`Accept: text/html` — DR-C4-10).
- **Posture env** — `SIG_API_RATE_LIMIT` = `off` (default — nothing
  mounted, the code ships dark ahead of the flip) · `advise` (headers +
  honest accounting, never rejects — the "defined" half) · `enforce`
  (the 429 rejection too — the "enforced" half);
  `SIG_API_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` (0–8, bounded) declares the trusted edge
  hops. An unknown posture refuses app construction loud — fail closed.
- **`app.py` mount order** — inside `BasisLabelMiddleware` (a rejection
  still carries `X-SIG-Basis` + the basis body field — the stamp survives
  the refusal) and inside the alias projection's caller side (a refused
  request burns no render work). The loopback curation app and the
  non-operational intake receiver are untouched — the limiter is the
  public read app's only (Part VIII §0.7).
- **`ops/gcp/rate-limit-enforcement.sh`** — the staged OM-20 flip:
  `--check` prints the plan with no ADC and no network (exit 0, now
  covered by the generic IaC test); `--apply` gates on ADC +
  `SIG_GCP_PROJECT` + `SIG_RATELIMIT_AUTHOR` (the recorded operator id —
  OM-20's scope discipline: silence is never consent) and the AR-3 daily
  freeze + batch-window guard (refuses exit 42); the prestate describe
  (env + `latestReadyRevisionName`) is the recorded restore point — the
  mutation itself is one bounded `gcloud run services update sig-api
  --update-env-vars SIG_API_RATE_LIMIT=enforce,SIG_API_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=2`;
  `--verify` reads the serving posture back. Rollback =
  `SIG_API_RATE_LIMIT=advise` (defined) or the prestate env verbatim.
- **Tests** — `tests/api/test_p36_13_rate_limit.py` (18): burst/rejection/
  headers on every path incl. errors, HTML rejection, trusted-hop key
  slicing + spoof resistance, client isolation, posture isolation
  (off/advise/enforce/env-driven/fail-closed), bucket mechanics, and
  curation+intake never gaining the middleware. Zero network.
- **Records** — `D-P36.13-1` (kind V, OPEN) + the `:e0`
  obligation-event anchor + the `return_pass.toml` map row (RETURN PASS
  region regenerated); the re-run prompt recorded verbatim:

## Deviations / deferrals

1. **The ticket's `SIG-API-009` label names a different spec row** —
   the canonical SIG-API-009 is the `/changes` feed (§37.3, MET via
   P14.1). The requirement this row lands is §37.4's anonymous-tier
   rate-limit clause (SIG-API-011) + K3 §5.6 / D-K3-6 [B-30]; the PR
   keeps the ticket's stamp and cites the canonical ids alongside. No
   coverage verdict changed; the spec-side reconciliation belongs to a
   spec_src amendment (SIG-ENG-003), never a hand-edit here.
2. **`SIG_API_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` is operator-declared** — 2 behind
   the Google external LB; a target not behind that LB sets the count
   it actually has. Client-claimed chain entries are never trusted
   (C4 NEW-16); a short chain falls back to the direct peer.
3. **Per-instance buckets** — Cloud Run instances count independently
   (no shared store — SIG-STORE-003). The bound is per-client
   per-instance — what the $0 in-process decision buys; a stricter
   global bound is exactly the edge layer D-K3-6 declined.
4. **The hosted-enforcement flip is queued** — `D-P36.13-1` (kind V,
   OPEN): `live_verification=false` dispatch + no
   ADC/`SIG_GCP_PROJECT` (OM-19). The GATE-G5 OM-20 naming
   (2026-10-25T18:40Z, expires GATE-G6) otherwise pre-authorises the
   flip inside `AR-3 + AR-2`; the staged runner + restore point are
   committed.
5. **Unhandled-exception stamping** — `ServerErrorMiddleware` sits
   outermost and bypasses inner send-wrappers on an unhandled raise;
   the middleware emits the stamped 500 itself when nothing started
   and re-raises for logging. A response already started can no
   longer gain headers — the same bound every middleware shares.
6. **obligation-events `append` workaround** — the per-call
   whole-chain validation deadlock the P36.76/77/78 rows recorded;
   the `:e0` anchor was appended as a JSONL line, `check` verified
   green (708 events).
